studies.Reference: Serum Iodine and Breast Cancer Risk: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study Stratified for Selenium Levels.
studies.Authors: Manjer J, Sandsveden M, Borgquist S
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.comparison_type: Above vs Below median iodine levels among women with high selenium
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Levels of baseline serum iodine and selenium were analyzed.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The current analysis included 1,159 breast cancer cases and 1,136 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: the OR for above versus below the median was 0.75 (0.57-0.99)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: high iodine levels were associated with a lower risk of breast cancer
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: the OR for above versus below the median was 0.75 (0.57-0.99)

studies.Reference: Blood Iodine as a Potential Marker of the Risk of Cancer in BRCA1 Carriers.
studies.Authors: Kiljańczyk A, Matuszczak M, Marciniak W, Derkacz R, Stempa K, Baszuk P, Bryśkiewicz M, Cybulski C, Dębniak T, Gronwald J, Huzarski T, Lener MR, Jakubowska A, Cheriyan A, Szwiec M, Stawicka-Niełacna M, Godlewski D, Prusaczyk A, Jasiewicz A, Kluz T, Tomiczek-Szwiec J, Kilar-Kobierzycka E, Siołek M, Wiśniowski R, Posmyk R, Jarkiewicz-Tretyn J, Sun P, Scott RJ, Narod SA, Lubiński J
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, we measured blood iodine levels

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We conducted a prospective study among 989 BRCA1 carriers
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: observed a negative association with breast cancer risk, with a significantly lower risk observed in quartile 4 (iodine > 38.0 µg/L) compared with quartile 1 (iodine < 30 µg/L)

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.68 (95% CI: 0.46–1.0), suggesting that iodine is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer. These findings were supported by moderate between-study heterogeneity (I² = 44.92%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.
